Our Mission

Four Goals of GYAC

  • 01Coaches teach the fundamentals of Olympic-style boxing
  • 02Provide an athletic diversion to drug use, gangs, and violence
  • 03Focus on self-esteem, goal-setting, discipline, respect, and personal responsibility
  • 04Handle life's triumphs and challenges outside of the boxing ring

In the Gym

The Work

About GYAC

More Than Boxing

GYAC provides a healthy environment for boys and girls ages 8 to 18 to learn the fundamentals of Olympic Style Boxing and to participate in Junior Olympic Boxing. Our open, inclusive atmosphere quickly forms lasting bonds between coaches, parents, youth, and older athletes.

GYAC also partners with Knox County Teen Court and the Knox County Probation office to work with youth who need mentoring and second chances.

"I was in seventh grade when we moved here, and honestly, I had a hard time fitting in. I started going to the GYAC with a friend of mine. Now, I bring her kid with me and my kid. It's been 21 years I've been coming here and I've learned so much." — Julie Guiste, Coach
"Carlos didn't write me off. I was 12 and plenty of folks did. But I got to come to a place where people saw me and accepted me." — Kelvin Medley, Former Participant & Current Coach

In Memoriam

Remembering Carlos Duncan

Adults called him by his first name. The kids knew him as Mr. D.

Boxing his entire life, GYAC was founded by his father Howard "Andy" Duncan and later managed by his brother before Carlos took over in the early 1990s. Mr. Duncan served in the U.S. Air Force and was a chairman for the U.S. Illinois Boxing Association Coaches Committee — a Certified Level IV elite coach, clinician, and official with U.S. Amateur Boxing Inc.

Carlos served on the boards for Knox County United Way, Knox County Teen Court, Knox County YMCA, Knox County Healthy Youth Alliance, and the Galesburg Youth Commission. He worked for Galesburg School District 205 and spent 12 years at the Literacy Coalition at Carl Sandburg College.

Carlos passed away on July 2, 2022 at the age of 80. He will always be remembered for his contributions to GYAC and the city of Galesburg.

The Program

Join the Gym

GYAC meets every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from 5:00 PM–7:00 PM. We are an Olympic Style Boxing program for ALL ages, with a primary focus on youth ages 8–18.

Code of Conduct

  • Be on time
  • Show respect to everyone in and out of the boxing area
  • Maintain at least a "C" average in school, or work with a tutor until grades improve
